message.content:
The only possible value is \(10\).

If \(M=0\), then \(\alpha=\beta=0\), which gives \(100=0\), impossible. So \(M>0\).

Write
\[
\alpha=Me^{i(\theta+\delta)},\qquad \beta=Me^{i(\theta-\delta)}
\]
for real \(\theta,\delta\). Let \(c=\cos\delta\in[-1,1]\) and \(z=Me^{i\theta}\). Then
\[
\alpha\beta=z^2,\qquad \alpha+\beta=2cz,
\]
so the given equation becomes
\[
z^2+2cz+100=0.
\]
Since \(c\) is real and \(|c|\le 1\), the discriminant is
\[
4c^2-400<0,
\]
so the two roots are nonreal conjugates. Their product is \(100\), hence for either root \(z\),
\[
|z|^2=z\overline z=100.
\]
Thus
\[
M=|z|=10.
\]

This value is attainable, e.g. \(\alpha=10,\ \beta=-10\).

\[
\boxed{10}
\]
